decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Save a bookmark — URL”; client round 1: “I approve the specification as-is.”
decisions.note: The specification directly supports saving a bookmark by URL; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “No auto-fetching of page titles or favicons (titles are user-entered)”; client round 1: “I approve the specification as-is.”
decisions.note: Automatic collection of required page metadata was explicitly excluded. The client's bare approval does not express awareness; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents only “URL, optional title & notes,” says “titles are user-entered,” and separately offers generic edit; client round 1 approves as-is.
decisions.note: The presented model omits description and does not provide editing of auto-collected title/description before and after saving. No difference was expressed; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 proposes “list all bookmarks” while explicitly excluding favicons and presenting no description field; client round 1 approves as-is.
decisions.note: The proposed list cannot expose the reference-required description and favicon per item. The client did not surface this difference; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “open a link”; client round 1 approves.
decisions.note: Opening a presented bookmark conforms to navigation to its original URL; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “keyword search (title/address/notes)”; client round 1: “I approve the specification as-is.”
decisions.note: The enumerated search fields omit description, which full-text search must cover. The approval does not identify the omission; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 defines bookmark input as “URL, optional title & notes,” adds tags separately, and proposes generic “Edit”; client round 1 approves as-is.
decisions.note: Description is absent from the presented bookmark data and therefore from the required editable field set. No correction was requested; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Edit & delete — with a confirmation step before removal”; client round 1 approves.
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion is supported; confirmation is an additional compatible behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Organize with tags — assign tags”; client round 1 approves.
decisions.note: Tag assignment conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “filter by [tags]”; client round 1 approves.
decisions.note: Filtering bookmarks by a selected tag conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “No browser import/export”; client round 1: “I approve the specification as-is.”
decisions.note: Netscape HTML import was explicitly excluded. Bare approval is not explicit acceptance of the difference; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “No browser import/export”; client round 1: “I approve the specification as-is.”
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export was explicitly excluded. This is separable from import and received no expressed disposition; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2: “Bookmarks and Tags, with a many-to-many link so a bookmark can carry several tags”; client round 2 approves the plan.
decisions.note: The planned many-to-many model supports one or more tags per bookmark; planning gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2: the tag model lets the user “filter by tag”; client round 2 approves.
decisions.note: The planned tag-filter behavior conforms; planning gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 initially lists “duplicate URLs” as an edge case; maker round 2 resolves it as “duplicate URLs warn but don't block”; client round 2: “The plan sounds appropriate. I approve it.”
decisions.note: The linked plan decision permits proceeding with a duplicate rather than converging on editing the existing bookmark. The client gave only general approval; planning gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 offers a “Suggested MVP scope” containing only US1 and says the client may “limit implementation to the MVP”; client round 3 selects “the full planned app, including all four user stories, rather than stopping at the MVP.”
decisions.note: The offered MVP alternative would omit otherwise conforming delete, link-opening, tag-assignment, and tag-filter behavior. The client explicitly selected the reference-closer full-scope alternative; task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US1 criterion: “save a bookmark, see it normalized & persisted”; client round 3 requests implementation of all stories.
decisions.note: The task breakdown retains URL-based saving; task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US2 criterion says only “list all”; the governing round-1 scope excludes favicons and has no description field. Client round 3 requests all four stories without addressing list contents.
decisions.note: The task-stage list still lacks the reference-required description/favicon presentation. Selecting all stories does not surface this field-level difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US2 criterion: “keyword filters,” carrying forward round 1's title/address/notes search; client round 3 requests all four stories without correcting search fields.
decisions.note: The task breakdown preserves search that omits description. The client's scope selection does not express this divergence; task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US2 criterion: “click opens in new tab”; client round 3 selects full implementation.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL in a new tab is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US3 criterion: “edit persists,” under the approved model with no description field; client round 3 asks for all stories but does not address editable fields.
decisions.note: The task-stage edit remains incomplete because description is absent. The response corrects implementation breadth, not this mismatch.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US3 criterion: “delete-after-confirm persists”; client round 3 selects full implementation.
decisions.note: The delete task conforms; task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US4 criterion: “tag two bookmarks”; client round 3 selects full implementation.
decisions.note: The task breakdown supports assigning tags to bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 US4 criterion: “filter by tag shows only those two”; client round 3 selects full implementation.
decisions.note: The task breakdown supports filtering to a selected tag's bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports “save with optional title/notes/tags” and successful API create/list verification; client round 4 accepts the app.
decisions.note: The implemented app supports saving bookmarks by URL; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 says the app was built “strictly against the approved spec” and reports manual “save with optional title,” while round 1 explicitly excluded auto-fetching; client round 4: “matches what I approved… I accept it.”
decisions.note: The implemented save flow preserves the explicit no-auto-metadata divergence. The final response is bare acceptance and does not state the difference; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports optional title/notes/tags and generic edit under the approved description-free, manually entered metadata model; client round 4 accepts it.
decisions.note: The implementation still lacks editable auto-collected title/description before and after saving. The client does not express that difference; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports the final list under the approved scope that excluded favicons and never introduced description; client round 4 says it “matches what I approved.”
decisions.note: The final list remains short of the required per-item description and favicon. General acceptance is not explicit acceptance of this divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 claims implemented “keyword search,” built strictly from the approved title/address/notes search; client round 4 accepts the app without mentioning search coverage.
decisions.note: Description remains outside full-text search. The final acceptance does not surface the mismatch; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports “open-in-new-tab” among implemented requirements; client round 4 accepts.
decisions.note: Opening the original bookmark URL in a new tab is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports implemented “edit” for the approved URL/title/notes/tags model, which has no description; client round 4 accepts without identifying the missing field.
decisions.note: The final edit behavior does not cover every required bookmark field. No corrective or explicitly accepting disposition was expressed.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports implemented “delete-with-confirmation”; client round 4 accepts.
decisions.note: The implemented deletion behavior conforms; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports saving with tags and tag filtering; client round 4 accepts.
decisions.note: Implemented tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports implemented “tag filtering”; client round 4 accepts.
decisions.note: Implemented filtering by a selected tag conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 reports a tested “non-blocking duplicate warning”; client round 4: “The completed app matches what I approved… I accept it.”
decisions.note: The implemented warning still allows duplicate saving instead of guiding the user into editing the existing item and preventing duplication. The client did not explicitly identify or accept that difference; implementation review.
